- [USER] User asked about the significance of the 1884 Electoral Reform Act in shaping the composition and powers of the Storting.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The 1884 Electoral Reform Act transformed the composition and powers of the Storting, the Norwegian parliament.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Before the 1884 Act, the Storting was dominated by wealthy landowners and elites resistant to democratic reforms.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Act introduced a more democratic electoral system that expanded the right to vote and allowed greater representation for the working class and rural populations.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The right to vote was broadened to all adult males who were 25 years or older and had lived in a district for at least two years.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Act introduced proportional representation, meaning the number of representatives a political party could have in the Storting was based on the share of the vote they received.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The 1884 Act granted the Storting greater powers, including the authority to make laws, levy taxes, and approve the budget.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Previously, the Storting’s powers were limited, and its ability to pass important reforms was constrained by the veto power of the king.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The 1884 Electoral Reform Act played a crucial role in democratizing Norwegian politics and creating a more representative and powerful Storting.
- [USER] User expressed interest in the topic and inquired about opposition to the 1884 Electoral Reform Act when it was first introduced.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] There was significant opposition to the 1884 Electoral Reform Act from conservatives and wealthy elites who saw it as a threat to their political power.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Opponents argued that expanding the right to vote and introducing proportional representation could lead to instability and radicalism in Norwegian politics.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Opponents feared that the interests of the urban working class would dominate the Storting over those of the conservative rural population.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Despite the opposition, the Act was passed and implemented, leading to significant positive effects on Norwegian democracy and governance.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Following the Act's passage, the Storting became a more representative and diverse body, able to pass important reforms benefiting a broader cross-section of Norwegian society.
